concept: Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling
summary: Source-anchored research for Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Streaming adds OP_MSG exhaustAllowed to awaitable hello. moreToCome permits successive replies without new requests; drivers process every reply in arrival order and send another awaitable request when a successful reply ends the stream. (low confidence)

SERVER-128517 describes very small pre-auth streamable-hello waits, especially zero, creating rapid server wakeups. The server implementation can clamp a requested wait to minWaitForStreamingHelloMillis or reject it when abortStreamingHelloWithSmallTimeout is enabled; deployments require version-specific verification. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

FaaS suspension can accumulate streamed heartbeats and force clients to process stale responses after resumption. This motivated the polling default; streaming also costs an additional RTT connection and thread per monitored server. (high confidence)

AWS documents that Lambda freezes an execution environment once the runtime and extensions finish and no events remain. Unfinished background callbacks or processes resume if Lambda reuses that environment; continuous monitor execution between invocations cannot be assumed. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

An awaited heartbeat may normally last about ten seconds with the default heartbeat interval. The awaited event field distinguishes intentional server waiting from a slow ordinary heartbeat; duration alone is not network RTT. (low confidence)

The FaaS polling default is scoped to supported driver monitoring modes, rather than a claim that streaming is universally unsuitable. Explicit serverMonitoringMode permits an override when platform detection is inaccurate or polling is preferable elsewhere. (high confidence)

Awaitable hello is discovered through topologyVersion in a hello response. Requests supply topologyVersion and maxAwaitTimeMS; the server replies on a processId mismatch, a greater topology counter, or expiry of the maximum wait. (high confidence)

serverMonitoringMode defaults to auto: detected FaaS uses poll, other environments use stream. Explicit poll forces polling; stream uses streaming only if supported, otherwise polling. Detection follows the handshake client.env rules. (high confidence)

Polling performs hello or legacy hello checks and sleeps heartbeatFrequencyMS between checks. Streaming instead begins the next read immediately after a successful response and sets maxAwaitTimeMS to heartbeatFrequencyMS. (high confidence)

Streaming measures RTT with periodic regular hello commands on a separate dedicated connection; streaming response duration must not update RTT. Polling must not create a dedicated RTT connection. (high confidence)
FaaS suspension can accumulate stale streaming heartbeats; DRIVERS-2578 also identifies socket timeouts after runtime resumption as motivation for polling. (high confidence)

NODE-6839 records a reconnection complaint after upgrading to Mongoose 8 and driver 6, but its resolution is Gone away with no fix version. It does not establish a confirmed current driver-wide regression. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-03-26)

Node.js timers define eligibility thresholds, not exact execution times. Starting with libuv 1.45.0 in Node.js 20, timers run after poll in each loop iteration, with a compatibility timer pass before entering the loop. Historical claims that timers always precede socket reads require runtime-specific qualification. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

For awaitable replies, a nonzero connectTimeoutMS becomes a socket timeout of connectTimeoutMS plus heartbeatFrequencyMS. A zero connectTimeoutMS remains unlimited, including awaitable replies. (low confidence)
